review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

16:1.sourceText: Καὶ διαγενομένου τοῦ σαββάτου Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ Σαλώμη ἠγόρασαν ἀρώματα ἵνα ἐλθοῦσαι ἀλείψωσιν αὐτόν.
16:1.targetText: When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so they could go and anoint the body of Jesus.

groups.note: The genitive absolute διαγενομένου τοῦ σαββάτου supplies the temporal clause.
The article ἡ with the genitive τοῦ Ἰακώβου ("the one of James") is rendered "the mother of James".
The participle ἐλθοῦσαι ("having come") is rendered as the coordinated verb go.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed; When belongs to the genitive absolute.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
English lists the names with a comma, so this καί has no separate English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἐλθοῦσαι is rendered as the verb go.
English supplies "the body of"; the Greek object is only αὐτόν ("him").

16:2.sourceText: καὶ λίαν πρωῒ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ἔρχονται ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα, ἀνατείλαντος τοῦ ἡλίου.
16:2.targetText: Very early on the first day of the week, just after sunrise, they went to the tomb.

groups.note: The feminine μιᾷ ("one") implies ἡμέρᾳ and is rendered as the ordinal "first".
BSB's Greek reads μνημεῖον here; both μνῆμα and μνημεῖον mean "tomb".
The genitive absolute ἀνατείλαντος τοῦ ἡλίου ("the sun having risen") is rendered "just after sunrise".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the noun day that the feminine μιᾷ implies; N1904 has no word for it.

16:3.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἑαυτάς Τίς ἀποκυλίσει ἡμῖν τὸν λίθον ἐκ τῆς θύρας τοῦ μνημείου;
16:3.targetText: They were asking one another, “Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?”

groups.note: The imperfect ἔλεγον ("were saying") introduces their question.
πρὸς ἑαυτάς ("to themselves") is rendered "one another".

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves ἡμῖν ("for us") unexpressed.

16:4.sourceText: καὶ ἀναβλέψασαι θεωροῦσιν ὅτι ἀνακεκύλισται ὁ λίθος· ἦν γὰρ μέγας σφόδρα.
16:4.targetText: But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, even though it was extremely large.

groups.note: This καί is contrastive; BSB renders it But.
The participle ἀναβλέψασαι is rendered as a when-clause.
BSB's Greek reads ἀποκεκύλισται here; both verbs mean the stone had been rolled away.
BSB renders the explanatory γάρ ("for") as the concessive "even though".

16:5.sourceText: καὶ εἰσελθοῦσαι εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον εἶδον νεανίσκον καθήμενον ἐν τοῖς δεξιοῖς περιβεβλημένον στολὴν λευκήν, καὶ ἐξεθαμβήθησαν.
16:5.targetText: When they entered the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side, and they were alarmed.

groups.note: εἰσελθοῦσαι εἰς ("having gone into") is rendered as a When-clause with the transitive verb entered.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed; When belongs to the participle.

16:6.sourceText: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐταῖς Μὴ ἐκθαμβεῖσθε· Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε τὸν Ναζαρηνὸν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον· ἠγέρθη, οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἴδε ὁ τόπος ὅπου ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.
16:6.targetText: But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here! See the place where they put Him.

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ works as the subject pronoun.

16:7.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ὑπάγετε εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ Πέτρῳ ὅτι Προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν· ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε, καθὼς εἶπεν ὑμῖν.
16:7.targetText: But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.’”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:8.sourceText: καὶ ἐξελθοῦσαι ἔφυγον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου, εἶχεν γὰρ αὐτὰς τρόμος καὶ ἔκστασις· καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν εἶπαν· ἐφοβοῦντο γάρ.
16:8.targetText: So the women left the tomb and ran away, trembling and bewildered. And in their fear they did not say a word to anyone.

groups.note: The participle ἐξελθοῦσαι ("having gone out") is rendered as the finite verb left.
The noun ἔκστασις ("amazement") is rendered as the adjective bewildered.
After the negated verb, οὐδενί ("to no one") is rendered "to anyone".
οὐδέν ("nothing") carries the negation, rendered "not … a word".
BSB recasts ἐφοβοῦντο γάρ ("for they were afraid") as the phrase "in their fear".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes the tomb the object of left, so ἀπό ("from") has no separate English word.
BSB recasts "for trembling and amazement had seized them" as "trembling and bewildered", so εἶχεν γὰρ αὐτάς has no separate English words.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the participle and verb ending.
English coordinator; the participle ἐξελθοῦσαι is rendered as the finite verb left.

16:9.sourceText: [[Ἀναστὰς δὲ πρωῒ πρώτῃ σαββάτου ἐφάνη πρῶτον Μαρίᾳ τῇ Μαγδαληνῇ, παρ’ ἧς ἐκβεβλήκει ἑπτὰ δαιμόνια.
16:9.targetText: Early on the first day of the week, after Jesus had risen, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had driven out seven demons.

groups.note: The participle ἀναστάς ("having risen") is rendered as an after-clause.
The dative πρώτῃ ("on the first") implies ἡμέρᾳ, "day".

English supplies the noun day that the feminine πρώτῃ implies; N1904 has no word for it.

16:10.sourceText: ἐκείνη πορευθεῖσα ἀπήγγειλεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ γενομένοις πενθοῦσι καὶ κλαίουσιν·
16:10.targetText: She went and told those who had been with Him, who were mourning and weeping.

groups.note: The article with the participle (τοῖς … γενομένοις) is rendered "those who had been".

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle πορευθεῖσα is rendered as the finite verb went.

16:11.sourceText: κἀκεῖνοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ζῇ καὶ ἐθεάθη ὑπ’ αὐτῆς ἠπίστησαν.
16:11.targetText: And when they heard that Jesus was alive and she had seen Him, they did not believe it.

groups.note: κἀκεῖνοι is καί + ἐκεῖνοι ("and those").
The participle ἀκούσαντες is rendered as a when-clause.
BSB turns the passive ἐθεάθη ("He was seen") into the active "had seen Him".
The agent phrase ὑπ’ αὐτῆς ("by her") becomes the subject of the active verb.
The verb ἠπίστησαν ("disbelieved") contains the negation.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending of ζῇ.
English supplies an object for "believe".

16:12.sourceText: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα δυσὶν ἐξ αὐτῶν περιπατοῦσιν ἐφανερώθη ἐν ἑτέρᾳ μορφῇ πορευομένοις εἰς ἀγρόν·
16:12.targetText: After this, Jesus appeared in a different form to two of them as they walked along in the country.

groups.note: The participle πορευομένοις ("going") is rendered by along, describing them as on their way.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

16:13.sourceText: κἀκεῖνοι ἀπελθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς λοιποῖς· οὐδὲ ἐκείνοις ἐπίστευσαν.
16:13.targetText: And they went back and reported it to the rest, but they did not believe them either.

groups.note: κἀκεῖνοι is καί + ἐκεῖνοι ("and those").
οὐδέ ("and not, nor") is rendered "but … not … either".

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἀπελθόντες is rendered as the finite verb went back.
English supplies an object for "reported".

16:14.sourceText: Ὕστερον δὲ ἀνακειμένοις αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐφανερώθη, καὶ ὠνείδισεν τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν καὶ σκληροκαρδίαν ὅτι τοῖς θεασαμένοις αὐτὸν ἐγηγερμένον οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν.
16:14.targetText: Later, as they were eating, Jesus appeared to the Eleven and rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen Him after He had risen.

groups.note: The participle ἀνακειμένοις ("reclining at table") is rendered as an as-clause.
αὐτοῖς refers to the Eleven, who are the subject of the English as-clause.
The article with the participle (τοῖς θεασαμένοις) is rendered "those who had seen".
The perfect participle ἐγηγερμένον ("raised") is rendered as an after-clause.

16:15.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορευθέντες εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἅπαντα κηρύξατε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον πάσῃ τῇ κτίσει.
16:15.targetText: And He said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.

16:16.sourceText: ὁ πιστεύσας καὶ βαπτισθεὶς σωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ἀπιστήσας κατακριθήσεται.
16:16.targetText: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.

groups.note: The article with the participle (ὁ πιστεύσας) is rendered "Whoever believes"; the same article also governs βαπτισθείς.
The article with the participle (ὁ ἀπιστήσας, "the one disbelieving") is rendered "whoever does not believe".

16:17.sourceText: σημεῖα δὲ τοῖς πιστεύσασιν ταῦτα παρακολουθήσει, ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δαιμόνια ἐκβαλοῦσιν, γλώσσαις λαλήσουσιν καιναῖς,
16:17.targetText: And these signs will accompany those who believe: In My name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues;

groups.note: The article with the participle (τοῖς πιστεύσασιν) is rendered "those who believe".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:18.sourceText: ὄφεις ἀροῦσιν κἂν θανάσιμόν τι πίωσιν οὐ μὴ αὐτοὺς βλάψῃ, ἐπὶ ἀρρώστους χεῖρας ἐπιθήσουσιν καὶ καλῶς ἕξουσιν.
16:18.targetText: they will pick up snakes with their hands, and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not harm them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will be made well.”

groups.note: κἄν is καί + ἐάν ("and if").
οὐ μή is an emphatic double negative, rendered "not".
The idiom καλῶς ἕξουσιν ("they will have it well") means they will recover.
